class.name: PhysXDestructible3D
class.brief_description: A mesh that fractures into real rigid-body debris at runtime, provided by the PhysX module's NvBlast integration.
class.description: Author one by selecting a [MeshInstance3D] and using [b]Mesh → Fracture with Blast[/b] (or right-clicking a [Mesh] resource in the FileSystem dock) -- a live in-viewport dialog lets you pick a fracture pattern and Accept replaces the node with a [PhysXDestructible3D] using the result, saved as a [member blast_asset] resource next to the scene. While intact, it renders and collides as the whole unfractured mesh through one [PhysicsServer3D] body. [method apply_radial_damage] breaks it explicitly -- an explosion, a weapon hit -- and each newly detached piece becomes its own real rigid body with a cooked convex collision hull, kicked outward from the damage origin at [member shatter_speed]. [member dynamic] additionally makes the intact object fall and collide like any other rigid body, and lets a hard enough physical impact fracture it on its own via [member impact_strength] / [member impact_damage_scale] / [member impact_radius], the way stacked destructible props behave in other engines' Blast integrations. [b]How damage, health, and radius actually interact:[/b] every bond holding two pieces of the mesh together starts with [member health] "hit points." A single [method apply_radial_damage] call applies its [code]damage[/code] amount [i]in full[/i] to every bond within [code]min_radius[/code] of the hit, falling off linearly to zero by [code]max_radius[/code] (nothing beyond that radius is touched at all). A bond breaks once the damage it has received -- from one hit or accumulated across several -- reaches its [member health]. So [code]damage >= health[/code] at full strength (inside [code]min_radius[/code]) breaks that bond outright in one hit; a weaker or more distant hit only chips at it, leaving it standing until a harder or closer follow-up (or several weaker ones) finishes the job. A piece only visibly detaches once every bond connecting it to the rest of the structure has broken -- a hit that weakens several bonds without fully breaking any of them can leave the object looking untouched even though it took real damage. [member dynamic]'s auto-fracture path feeds the exact same pipeline: a collision whose impulse clears [member impact_strength] is converted to [code]damage = (impulse - impact_strength) * impact_damage_scale[/code] (floored so it always at least matches [member health] × 1.5, guaranteeing a real break rather than a hit that looked hard but silently did nothing) and applied via [method apply_radial_damage] at the contact point with [code]min_radius = 0[/code] and [code]max_radius = [/code][member impact_radius]. [b]Mass:[/b] [member auto_mass] computes a default from the intact mesh's real volume × a fixed internal density (~2200 kg/m³, roughly concrete) -- read-only in the Inspector while it's on, so it shows what the object would actually weigh. Uncheck it for a true, freely-editable override. Either way, [member mass] is the [i]whole intact object's[/i] mass; once fractured, each piece gets a share of it proportional to its own volume, not a flat split.

method.name: apply_radial_damage
method.description: Applies [param damage] to every bond within [param max_radius] of [param world_position], at full strength inside [param min_radius] and falling off linearly to zero at [param max_radius]. A bond breaks once its cumulative received damage reaches [member health]; a piece detaches (spawning a real rigid body) once every bond connecting it to the rest of the structure has broken. Works identically whether [member dynamic] is [code]true[/code] or [code]false[/code] -- it doesn't require the object to be falling or moving, so a fixed static prop is fully breakable this way (see [member dynamic]'s own note). Returns how many new pieces this call actually detached; [code]0[/code] means the hit landed (in range) but wasn't enough to break anything. Each newly detached piece gets a real outward velocity -- radial direction from [param world_position] to that piece's own centroid, scaled by [member shatter_speed] and the same distance falloff the damage itself used, plus a slight upward bias.

members.member: Legacy loading path: a [code].asset[/code] file (raw [code]NvBlastAsset[/code] bytes), paired with [member chunks_path]. Prefer [member blast_asset] for anything authored through the in-editor fracture dialog; this remains only for assets authored before [PhysXBlastAsset] existed as a real [Resource] type.

When [code]true[/code], [member mass] is recomputed from the intact mesh's real volume (times its node scale) every time the asset (re)loads, and shown read-only in the Inspector -- "here's what this object would actually weigh." Uncheck it for a true, freely-editable override that survives reloads; checking it again immediately recomputes fresh and discards that override.
The fractured mesh data to use, saved by the in-editor fracture dialog (or [PhysXBlastAuthoring] directly). Preferred over [member asset_path] / [member chunks_path] when set.

Shadow-casting behavior for every piece's render mesh, the same four settings as [member GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow]. Applies uniformly, intact or fractured -- changing it re-pushes to every already-existing piece immediately.
Legacy loading path: a [code].chunks[/code] text file (per-chunk render-mesh triangle soup), paired with [member asset_path]. See [member asset_path]'s own note.

Physics layers this object (intact or fractured) occupies, same meaning as [member RigidBody3D.collision_layer]. Applies to every body this class creates -- changing this after pieces already exist immediately updates all of them, the same as a real [RigidBody3D] would.
Physics layers this object (intact or fractured) collides with, same meaning as [member RigidBody3D.collision_mask]. See [member collision_layer]'s own note on when a change takes effect.

When [code]true[/code], the intact object is a real falling/colliding rigid body instead of a fixed prop, and a hard enough physical collision auto-fractures it (see [member impact_strength] / [member impact_damage_scale] / [member impact_radius]). When [code]false[/code] (the default), it stays a fixed prop that only ever breaks from an explicit [method apply_radial_damage] call -- including from an explosion or weapon script, so a static object is still fully breakable, it just can't fracture itself by physically colliding into something.
Widens the bounds used for frustum culling on every piece, the same as [member GeometryInstance3D.extra_cull_margin]. Raise it if a fast-moving piece pops in/out of view near the screen edge.

Controls VoxelGI baking for every piece's render mesh, the same two settings as [member GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode]. Defaults to [constant GI_MODE_STATIC], matching a plain [MeshInstance3D]'s default. Consider [constant GI_MODE_DYNAMIC] for an object that's expected to move once fractured -- but a single fracture can spawn many pieces at once, and a VoxelGI's dynamic-object tracking cost scales with how many it has to follow every frame, so it isn't the default.

How much cumulative damage each bond in the fracture structure can absorb before it breaks -- see the class description's "How damage, health, and radius actually interact" section for the full picture. Higher [member health] needs more damage (a harder hit, a closer one, or several weaker ones added together) to break the same bond.
When [code]true[/code], every piece is exempt from occlusion culling, the same as [member GeometryInstance3D.ignore_occlusion_culling].

[member dynamic]-only. Once a collision's impulse clears [member impact_strength], this scales how much extra damage the excess produces: [code]damage = (impulse - impact_strength) * impact_damage_scale[/code] (before the [member health] × 1.5 floor -- see [method apply_radial_damage]'s note). Raise it so impacts that do clear the threshold break things more decisively; it has no effect on whether an impact counts as a hit at all, only on how much damage a qualifying one deals.

[member dynamic]-only. The [code]max_radius[/code] passed to the auto-triggered [method apply_radial_damage] call on a qualifying impact, centered on the contact point ([code]min_radius[/code] is always [code]0[/code] for this path -- full damage right at the contact, falling off to [member impact_radius]). How far a hard impact's damage reaches into the rest of the object, not how hard the impact needs to be.

[member dynamic]-only. The minimum contact impulse (roughly mass × velocity change, in Godot's physics units) that counts as an impact worth reacting to at all -- landing softly or a gentle bump below this is ignored entirely, no damage applied. Raise it to make the object tolerate harder knocks before it can self-fracture; it has no effect on how much damage a qualifying impact deals (see [member impact_damage_scale] for that).

A piece (fractured debris, or the intact body itself if [member dynamic]) whose world-space Y position falls below this is freed automatically. Bounds memory/body count for a scene where something can fall indefinitely -- no floor everywhere, a gap, missing the pile entirely -- instead of debris simulating forever off in the void. The default is low enough not to trigger in an ordinary scene; set it to match this scene's actual floor or void.
Mesh LOD selection bias for every piece, the same as [member GeometryInstance3D.lod_bias]. Higher values keep more detail at a distance.

The whole intact object's mass, same meaning as [member RigidBody3D.mass]. Read-only while [member auto_mass] is on (see its own note). Once fractured, each piece gets a share of this proportional to its own volume -- a large remaining chunk and a tiny sliver don't get the same weight.

A second material layered on top of every piece's render mesh, the same as [member GeometryInstance3D.material_overlay] -- decals, damage overlays, and the like, without replacing the base material the way [member material_override] does.
Material applied to every piece's render mesh, intact or fractured, in place of the source mesh's own materials (which aren't carried over by the fracture process).

Speed (m/s, before falloff) each newly detached piece is kicked away from the damage origin -- see [method apply_radial_damage]'s own note on the exact direction/falloff shape. Purely a "how violently does debris scatter on break" feel knob, not a physically derived value.
Distance from the camera at which every piece starts being visible, the same as [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begin]. [code]0.0[/code] disables the near limit.

Fade transition distance for [member visibility_range_begin], the same as [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begin_margin]. Only has an effect when [member visibility_range_fade_mode] isn't [constant VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_DISABLED].
Distance from the camera beyond which every piece stops being visible, the same as [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end]. [code]0.0[/code] disables the far limit.
Fade transition distance for [member visibility_range_end], the same as [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end_margin]. See [member visibility_range_begin_margin]'s own note.
How pieces fade in/out at the edges of [member visibility_range_begin]/[member visibility_range_end], the same as [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_fade_mode].

constants.constant: Pieces neither receive nor are captured by baked or dynamic GI.
Pieces are treated as static geometry for GI purposes, matching a plain [MeshInstance3D]'s default. The default for [member gi_mode].
Pieces are tracked as dynamic objects by a [VoxelGI] as they move. See [member gi_mode]'s own note on the cost tradeoff before enabling this broadly.
Pieces cast normal shadows. The default for [member cast_shadow].
Pieces cast shadows from both faces, as if double-sided, regardless of the mesh's actual winding.
Pieces are invisible themselves but still cast shadows.
No fade -- pieces simply pop in/out at [member visibility_range_begin]/[member visibility_range_end]. The default for [member visibility_range_fade_mode].
Each piece fades its own alpha in/out at the visibility range edges.
Pieces this object is visually linked to (via a shared LOD group) fade together instead of independently.
